metadata.note: The Wallkill Valley Railroad ran from Kingston, NY south through the Wallkill Valley (Rosendale, New Paltz, Gardiner, Wallkill, Walden, Montgomery) to a leased connection with the Erie Railroad at Campbell Hall, giving Ulster and Orange County farms and villages a route to New York City via the Erie. Passenger service ran 1870-1937. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap: this corridor is unusually well preserved -- almost the entire route (including the well-known Rosendale trestle) is now the Wallkill Valley Rail Trail, so every hop resolved to a connected, plausible real path with no straight-line fallbacks needed anywhere on the route.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallkill_Valley_Railroad (chartered April 26 1866; reached New Paltz and formally opened December 20 1870; Rosendale trestle built by 1872, reached Kingston by end of 1872; leased to the Erie Railroad for its first 10 years; Erie's Montgomery-Campbell Hall branch leased to the Wallkill Valley; passenger service abandoned 1937; last regular freight run December 31 1977; station list Kingston-Whiteport-Binnewater-Rosendale-Springtown-New Paltz-Forest Glen-Gardiner-New Hurley-Wallkill-Walden-Montgomery-Campbell Hall)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallkill_Valley_Rail_Trail (modern rail-trail preserving almost the entire historic right-of-way)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API): former-railway/rail-trail (Wallkill Valley Rail Trail) and abandoned/disused railway tagging for the full Kingston-Rosendale-New Paltz-Gardiner-Wallkill-Walden-Montgomery-Campbell Hall corridor; routed via Dijkstra shortest path through a graph of real track/trail ways between each station's geocoded (Nominatim/OSM) coordinates, with no straight-line fallbacks needed anywhere on the route.

segments.note: Chartered April 26, 1866; reached New Paltz and formally opened December 20, 1870; extended north via the Rosendale trestle (built by 1872) to Kingston by the end of 1872. Leased to the Erie Railroad for its first 10 years, which also built a branch Montgomery-Campbell Hall (leased to the Wallkill Valley), giving through connections to the Erie Railroad and onward to New Jersey/New York City. Built primarily to carry produce, milk, and passengers to this Erie interchange. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
